amendments.change: New V39 only (free after current V38; recheck immediately before implementation). Three new Identity tables and guard/helper functions; canonical grants/proofs/outbox/audit/activation receipts retained. Existing migrations byte-unchanged.

Add provenance/transition/deferred-evidence guards on marked Admin user_account/account_grant/action_proof/invitation_outbox and mutual-exclusion guards with customer_identifier/local_staff_principal/merchant.membership. No existing Customer/Staff/IAM rows rewritten; runtime cannot direct-write marked identity/grants/receipt. Lock order population -> request serialization -> realm -> account -> proof/receipt; no cross-owner lock inversion.

Finite new SQL privileges: writer SELECT necessary existing Identity rows; INSERT pending account/grants/proof/outbox/audit/receipt; column-limited UPDATE credential/state/version/proof/outbox; DELETE only marked Admin grants within guarded replace/revoke. No TRUNCATE, realm UPDATE, DDL, owner role or Support/Merchant/Finance grants. Runtime only admitted boolean read + guarded SQL09, plus existing constrained session/outbox operations. PUBLIC denied all new objects by default. Runtime/guard callers get only SQL19/20 boolean EXECUTE, no SELECT on private marker/environment/operator receipts.

Optional V40 extends receipt operation allowlist, adds explicit pre-activation bootstrap-only outbox/acceptance eligibility. Ordinary existing management invitations still require ACTIVE realm, and Admin invitations always require ACTIVE realm. No general INACTIVE exception; initial Root state/grants managed only through existing V4 checks plus explicit wrapper scope.

New authority roles are registered by separately approved privileged isolated-cluster prerequisites, never CREATE ROLE in Flyway; no automatic membership to migrator/runtime or developer. Exact prerequisite generator must preserve existing pinned ownership/lifecycle/bootstrap collector functions; any hook delta separately explicit in implementation review.

New browser route /admin/activate captures fragment before auth restore/analytics, immediately scrubs history, keeps proof/token in memory; success redirects to /admin/login, no automatic session. No changes to six Dashboard APIs or Customer/Staff activation routes.

Isolated privileged prerequisites additionally grant EXECUTE pg_catalog.pg_control_system() only to identity_admin_writer and existing schema owner; runtime/operator get boolean predicate only. No writer SET/INHERIT to runtime/operator. Optional V40 bounded wrapper functions owned by Identity schema owner are the sole exception, not schema-owner login or general SQL executor.

replay_and_integrity.authorization: Recheck current nonsuperuser session_user membership, bound environment/realm and allowed target before receipt access. User strings/GUC/SET ROLE alone confer nothing. Persist and compare current login role OID as well as name; role-name reuse alone cannot authorize a receipt.
replay_and_integrity.digest: SHA256 of versioned canonical operation+deployment+realm+target+expectedVersion+sorted exact permissions+canonical validated input+reason; operator/session_user and request binding persisted. No password/secret in offline command.
replay_and_integrity.replay: Same request+same operator/input returns committed metadata with current state, before stale expectedVersion or consumed-proof rejection; different input conflict; different/revoked operator deny. Replay after revoke/disable never creates grant/proof/activation.
replay_and_integrity.atomicity: Account/marker/grants/proof/protected intent/audit/receipt in one physical transaction; receipt and deferred evidence cannot be forged by runtime/direct DML. Failure rolls back all; SMTP outside transaction.
replay_and_integrity.crypto_trust: Existing Identity application authenticates HMAC proof and PasswordPolicy before guarded SQL activation. SQL enforces relational/provenance consistency, not possession of an external HMAC key. Do not claim DB CHECKs verify raw tokens; compromised application/key-holder remains outside DB-only disclosure protection.
replay_and_integrity.digest_encoding: Authoritative SQL digest: sha256(convert_to(jsonb_build_object('v',1,'operation',operation,'deploymentId',deployment_id,'databaseName',current_database(),'realmId',realm_id,'targetId',target_id,'expectedVersion',expected_version,'displayName',display_name,'email',email,'permissions',sorted_permissions,'action',action,'reason',reason)::text,'UTF8')). Inapplicable keys remain JSON null, permissions sorted C, no normalization. Java never supplies a trusted digest. Request ID is the durable receipt PK/correlation, not authority and not part of the payload hash.
